Verse 1 Keep thy foot - This verse the Hebrew and all the versions join to the preceding chapter. "They offer gifts for their sins, and do not turn from their evil works; for they know not (they distinguish not) between good and evil." See the Chaldee.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen25454" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25455" type="x-p"/> Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, etc. - We are under constant obligations to live to God; no vow can make it more so. Yet, there may be cases in which we should bind ourselves to take up some particular cross, to perform some particular duty, to forego some particular attachment that does not tend to bring our souls nearer to God. Then, if fully determined, and strong in faith relative to the point, bind and hold fast; but if not fully, rationally, and conscientiously determined, "do not suffer thy mouth to cause thy soul to sin."

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen25455" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25456" type="x-p"/> Neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error - Nor think of saying "before the cruel angel, who shall exercise authority over thee in the judgment of the great day, that thou didst it through ignorance." - Chaldee. entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen25456" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25457" type="x-p"/> In - dreams - are - divers vanities; but fear thou God - If, by the disturbed state of thy mind during the day, or by Satanic influence, thou dream of evil, do not give way to any unreasonable fears, or gloomy forebodings, of any coming mischief: - Fear God. Fear neither the dream nor its interpretation; God, will take care of and protect thee. Most certainly, he that fears God need fear nothing else. Well may an upright soul say to Satan himself, I fear God; and because I fear him, I do not fear thee.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen25465" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25466" type="x-p"/> The profit of the earth is for all - The earth, if properly cultivated, is capable of producing food for every living creature; and without cultivation none has a right to expect bread. <div eID="gen25466" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25467" type="x-p"/> The king himself is served by the field - Without the field he cannot have supplies for his own house; and, unless agriculture flourish, the necessary expenses of the state cannot be defrayed. Thus, God joins the head and feet together; for while the peasant is protected by the king as executor of the laws, the king himself is dependent on the peasant; as the wealth of the nation is the fruit of the laborer's toil.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen25469" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25470" type="x-p"/> When goods increase - An increase of property always brings an increase of expense, by a multitude of servants; and the owner really possesses no more, and probably enjoys much less, than he did, when every day provided its own bread, and could lay up no store for the next. But if he have more enjoyment, his cares are multiplied; and he has no kind of profit. "This also is vanity."

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 13</hi> <div eID="gen25471" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25472" type="x-p"/> Riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt - This may be the case through various causes: <div eID="gen25472" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25473" type="x-p"/> 1. He may join in an unfortunate partnership and lose all. <div eID="gen25474" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25475" type="x-p"/> 3. entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 17</hi> <div eID="gen25478" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25479" type="x-p"/> All his days also he eateth in darkness - Even his enjoyments are embittered by uncertainty. He fears for his goods; the possibility of being deprived of them fills his heart with anguish. But instead of יאכל yochel, "he shall eat," ילך yelech, "he shall walk," is the reading of several MSS. He walks in darkness - he has no evidence of salvation. There is no ray of light from God to penetrate the gloom; and all beyond life is darkness impenetrable! <div eID="gen25479" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25480" type="x-p"/> And wrath with his sickness - His last hours are awful; for, "Counting on long years of pleasure here, <div eID="gen25480" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25481" type="x-p"/> He's quite unfurnish'd for the world to come." <div eID="gen25481" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25482" type="x-p"/> Blair. <div eID="gen25482" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen25483" type="x-p"/> He is full of anguish at the thought of death; but the fear of it is horrible. But if he have a sense of God's wrath in his guilty conscience, what horror can be compared with his horror!
